§10.4.4 Fill-Ins

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

forms-fill-ins · forms

✅ Normative

Each printed entry field MUST be rendered as one line. An empty field MUST be rendered as [blank] and MUST NOT be omitted.

The blank is the word marker [blank], like the protocol's other markers ([signature], [seal], [stamp]). It replaces the older [___], whose underscores pair up as emphasis whenever two blanks share a line (from [___] to [___]) and vanish when the Markdown is rendered. A printed bracketed word [blank] on the page is escaped, \[blank\] — see Escaping Printed Marks§7.2.4.

- \[1\] **Wages, tips, other compensation**: 29,513
- \[7\] **Social security tips**: [blank]
- \[9\]: [blank]

The shapes

The page prints Output
id + label + value - \[1\] **Label**: value
id, no label (shaded or unused boxes) - \[9\]: [blank]
neither id nor label, filled the bare value
neither id nor label, empty a bare [blank]

An empty field is content

An empty field says this was asked and not answered. Dropping it loses that, and the field count no longer matches the form — on a W-2 that is boxes 7–11, on a 1040 page 2 most of lines 17–31.

Adjacent boxes are separate fields

Two entry boxes printed side by side under one id are two fields and MUST NOT be fused into one value. W-2 box 15 prints State and Employer's state ID number side by side:

- \[15\]
  - **State**: SC
  - **Employer's state ID number**: 00-0000056

A currency glyph before a blank

A currency glyph printed before an empty field MUST be kept immediately before the blank — $[blank] — with any printed spacing preserved. The field's label MUST stay unchanged: the glyph is not folded into it.

✅ Sample — $ in empty cells

Every value cell in the Part III grids prints a $ and nothing else; two print N/A. Each $ cell is an empty field with its glyph kept: $[blank].

A field printed as several ruled lines

One answer field MUST be rendered as one [blank], however many ruled writing lines it offers. Separate blanks MUST be emitted only for fields that are separately labelled or independently answerable.

✅ Sample — numbered answer areas of four lines each

Items 24, 25 and 26 each print four ruled lines, then three checkbox lines, the last with a blank inside its sentence (OBJECTION# ______ listed above). Each item's four lines are one field.

Values printed before anyone fills the form

A preprinted or computed value MUST be transcribed exactly as printed, including 0 % and 0.00. A visible value MUST NOT be replaced with a blank.

✅ Sample — computed zeros in an unfilled invoice

Yellow input cells sit empty; every item row prints 0 % under % Total Budget and % Spent To Date, and the total rows print 0.00. A [A] reference tag sits beside the first total.

A label with no blank after it

An empty entry label such as Signed: or Date: MUST be followed by [blank] when the surrounding form clearly asks for that value, even though no line, box or space is drawn. A field MUST NOT be inferred from a colon in ordinary prose.

✅ Sample — signature lines with no line

Corresponding Author: with Signed: and Date: nested beneath it, each followed by a run of dashes and no ruled line or box. Each is an empty field.
